posts.topic: A price for everything, a reason for nothing
posts.why: Every food vendor recognises their own menu board in three seconds.

tiktok.hook: This menu has a price for everything and a reason for nothing.
beats: Add one line under each item
What is in it, who it feeds
Now the price has a job
tiktok.vo: This menu has a price for everything and a reason for nothing. Jollof, two thousand five hundred. Chicken, three thousand. Now add one line under each item: what is in it, and who it actually feeds. Rice, two pieces, one person, very hungry. Now the price has a job, and nobody has to ask you a question before they decide.
tiktok.cap: A price without a reason is a question. One line under each item answers it before it is asked.

slides: Say what is in it and who it feeds
Now the price has a job
instagram.cap: Your menu is a sales page. Give every price a reason and the questions stop.

facebook.body:
Look at your menu, price list or catalogue. Every item has a number and no reason.

Jollof, ₦2,500. Chicken, ₦3,000. A customer has to ask what is in it, how big it is, and whether it feeds one person or four. You answer that question forty times a day.

Add one line under each item: what is in it and who it feeds. Rice, two pieces, one hungry person.

The price does not change. The number of questions does.

What is the item you answer the most questions about?

posts.topic: 'How much?' is not a price question
posts.why: A reframe that turns a defensive moment into a useful one.

tiktok.hook: "How much?" is not a price question.
beats: It is: is this for me?
They cannot see the value yet
Give the context before the number
tiktok.vo: How much is not a price question. It is, is this for me. They cannot see what they are paying for yet, so any number looks like a lot. Give one line of context before the price and watch the same number land differently.
tiktok.cap: Nobody can judge a price without knowing what it is for.

instagram.cap: One line of context before your price changes how it is heard.

facebook.body:
When a customer asks 'how much?', we hear a price question. It is not.

It is 'is this for me?' They cannot see what they would be paying for, so every number looks big.

Give one line of context before the price: what it is, who it is for, what happens after. The same number lands completely differently.

What is your one line of context?

posts.topic: Say the price once, early
posts.why: A habit change that removes the most common customer question.

tiktok.hook: Hidden prices read as expensive and negotiable, not premium.
beats: They must message to find out
Say it early, say it once
tiktok.vo: Hiding your price does not make you look premium. It makes you look expensive and negotiable at the same time. A stranger assumes the worst number and does not bother asking. Say the price early, in the first three lines. The people who cannot afford it stop wasting your evening, and the ones who can finally get to the point.
tiktok.cap: Hidden price = expensive and negotiable. Both at once.

slides: Say it in the first three lines
instagram.cap: You are not hiding the price from competitors. You are hiding it from buyers.

facebook.body:
A lot of businesses hide their prices to look premium. It does not work that way.

No price reads as two things at once: too expensive for me, and negotiable. A stranger assumes the worst and does not ask.

Say the price early and say it once. The people who cannot afford it stop wasting your evening. The ones who can get straight to the point.

Do you show prices? Why or why not?

posts.topic: Discounting is the most expensive way to feel busy
posts.why: A position that will get disagreement in the comments, which is the point.

tiktok.hook: Discounting is the most expensive way to feel busy.
beats: Then a price you cannot raise
tiktok.vo: Discounting is the most expensive way to feel busy. You get more orders and the same money, then more work for less, then a customer who only buys on sale. Then one day you try to raise the price back and the same people tell you it is too expensive. You trained them.
tiktok.cap: You can train a customer to wait for a discount. You cannot easily untrain them.

slides: A customer who only buys on sale
instagram.cap: Discount when you have dead stock. Not to feel wanted.

facebook.body:
A small business I know discounts every December. More orders, same profit, twice the work.

Worse, they trained their customers. Now nobody buys at the normal price, because they know January is coming.

Discount dead stock. Discount a slot that would otherwise be empty. Do not discount to feel wanted.

When was the last time a discount actually made you money?

posts.topic: The tailor who raised his prices
posts.why: A counter-intuitive story that gives permission to stop competing on cheap.

tiktok.hook: A tailor raised his prices and got more orders.
beats: He was the cheapest on the street
He doubled the price, then delivered on time
tiktok.vo: A tailor I know was the cheapest on his street and could not fill his week. We asked what he would charge if he had to deliver in five days, every time. He doubled it. Same customers, different ones. The low price had been telling people he was not serious, and seriousness is what you are actually buying when you order a suit.
tiktok.cap: The low price was not attracting customers. It was filtering out the good ones.

instagram.cap: Cheap is a message. Make sure it is the one you meant to send.

facebook.body:
A tailor I know was the cheapest on his street and still had an empty week.

We asked what he would charge if he could promise five-day delivery, every time. He doubled it. He got fewer enquiries and more orders, from people who did not haggle.

The low price was not attracting customers. It was telling them he was not serious.

When did cheap stop working for you?

posts.topic: The quote is price, scope, date
posts.why: The most copied line of the month, applied to the harder document.

tiktok.hook: A quote with no date is a question they cannot answer.
tiktok.vo: A quote with no date is a question, and nobody can say yes to a question. Five lines: the price, what is included, what is not included, the date it will be finished, and one sentence they can reply yes to. The what is not included line is the one that wins the job, because it is the only line that sounds honest.
tiktok.cap: Price, scope, exclusions, date, one yes-shaped question.

instagram.cap: The exclusions line wins more jobs than the price does.

facebook.body:
Most quotes are one line: a number and 'let me know'.

That is a question, and a customer cannot say yes to a question.

Five lines: the price, what is included, what is not included, when it will be finished, and one sentence they can reply to. 'Shall I book the slot?'

The line about what is not included wins more jobs than the price, because it is the only one that sounds honest.

What does your quote look like right now?

posts.topic: Budget? Any budget.
posts.why: The exact meeting everyone has sat through.

tiktok.hook: Me: what is your budget? Client: any budget.
tiktok.vo: What is your budget. Any budget. That is not a budget, that is a hope. So do not ask. Give three options at three prices and one recommendation. People who do not know what things cost can still choose between three things.
tiktok.cap: Never ask for a budget. Offer three prices and one opinion.

instagram.cap: Choosing between three things is easy. Naming a number from nothing is not.

facebook.body:
'What is your budget?'

'Any budget.'

This conversation happens every day in Lagos, and it wastes a week.

People who do not know what things cost cannot name a number. They can, however, choose between three things. Give three options, three prices, and one recommendation.

You will get an answer in five minutes.

What do you do when a customer says 'any budget'?

posts.topic: Would you pay more for the fast one?
posts.why: The street answers do the arguing for you.

tiktok.hook: Would you pay more for the business that answers fast?
tiktok.vo: Would you pay more for the business that answers fast? Yes, said almost everyone. Then I asked how much more. Nobody had a number. Not one person had ever been asked, by any business, to pay for a reply. Which means if you are fast, you are giving it away.
tiktok.cap: Everyone will pay for speed. Nobody has ever been asked to.

instagram.cap: Speed is the only thing you can charge for that costs you nothing but attention.

facebook.body:
I asked people on the street: would you pay more for the business that answers fast?

Almost everyone said yes. Then I asked how much more. Nobody had a number.

Not one person had ever been asked. Which means the fast businesses are giving that advantage away for free, and losing the sale anyway to whoever replied first.

Reply fast. And maybe say so.

What is your reply time right now?

posts.topic: ₦5,000 is not cheap, it is small
posts.why: Reframing price as time, which is the only currency they are short of.

tiktok.hook: Five thousand is less than a plate of food for two.
beats: It is one afternoon of writing
Or spend three evenings learning it
tiktok.vo: Five thousand naira is less than a plate of food for two people. That does not make it cheap. But it is one afternoon of writing and designing, priced like a download. Or you can spend three evenings working it out yourself, badly, and redo it in January. You are not buying paper. You are buying the afternoon.
tiktok.cap: Nine packs, ₦5,000 each. For your own business. Message the keyword on WhatsApp: 0905 069 0837.

instagram.cap: It is one afternoon of work you do not have to repeat. ₦5,000. Message SILENCE on WhatsApp: 0905 069 0837.

facebook.body:
₦5,000 is less than a plate of food for two. That does not make my packs cheap. It makes them small.

What you are actually buying is an afternoon of writing and designing that you would otherwise spend three evenings doing badly, then redo in January.

The honest limit: these are do-it-yourself files. No consulting, no custom work, no guarantee of results. If you want it done for you, that is a project, not a download.

Nine packs at ₦5,000. Message SILENCE on WhatsApp: 0905 069 0837.

Which afternoon would you rather have back?

posts.topic: Match this ₦20,000 quote
posts.why: A story about what cheap really buys, from the inside.

tiktok.hook: Someone asked us to match a ₦20,000 website quote.
beats: Not because we are too proud
So we showed them half a day
tiktok.vo: Someone asked us to match a twenty thousand naira website quote. We said we cannot, and it was not pride. Twenty thousand is half a day of work, so we told them what half a day buys: one page, one offer, one button, no CMS. They took it. The other quote had been selling them something nobody could deliver.
tiktok.cap: We did not say no. We said what ₦20,000 is, honestly.

instagram.cap: A quote you cannot deliver is not a bargain. It is a refund with extra steps.

facebook.body:
Someone asked us to match a ₦20,000 website quote.

We said we cannot, and it was not pride. ₦20,000 is half a day of work. So we told them exactly what half a day buys: one page, one offer, one button, no CMS.

They took it.

The other quote had been selling them a site nobody could build in half a day. Which means somewhere in the next two months, they would have found that out.

Have you ever been quoted something that sounded too good?

posts.topic: Never quote a range
posts.why: One line that removes an entire negotiation.

tiktok.hook: Never quote a range in a first reply.
tiktok.vo: Never quote a range in a first reply. Fifty to eighty thousand is heard as fifty thousand, and everything above it becomes a negotiation. If the price depends on the job, quote the smallest version and describe it. Otherwise quote one number and stand behind it.
tiktok.cap: A range is a discount you have already given.

instagram.cap: Quote the smallest version, or quote one number. Not a range.

facebook.body:
Never quote a range in a first reply.

'₦50,000 to ₦80,000' is heard as ₦50,000. Everything above that becomes a negotiation you did not agree to have, and you usually lose it because you already said the number.

If the price really depends on the job, quote the smallest version and describe what that gets them. Otherwise quote one number and stand behind it.

Have you ever quoted a range and regretted it?

posts.topic: Nine seconds to load
posts.why: Almost everyone can check this on their own site tonight.

tiktok.hook: This page takes nine seconds to load on mobile data.
beats: Nine seconds is a bus ride
tiktok.vo: This page takes nine seconds to load on mobile data. Nine seconds is long enough to open another tab, get distracted, and buy from someone else. The cause is almost always two images that were never compressed. Run them through a compressor before uploading and this page is under three seconds.
tiktok.cap: Nine seconds is not slow. Nine seconds is a customer leaving.

instagram.cap: Most slow sites are one enormous photo wearing a nice dress.

facebook.body:
Open your site on mobile data, not wifi, and count the seconds.

Nine seconds is long enough for a customer to open another tab and buy from someone else.

The cause is almost always one or two photos straight from a phone camera, four megabytes each, uploaded at full size. Compress them before uploading and most pages drop under three seconds.

It is a ten minute fix that has been costing you for a year.

How fast is yours?

posts.topic: Built on a laptop, seen on a phone
posts.why: The single most common design failure in Lagos.

tiktok.hook: Your site was built on a laptop. They are holding a phone.
tiktok.vo: Your site was designed on a laptop and your customer is holding a phone in one hand, in traffic. Different screen, different distance, different attention. Look at your own page on the cheapest Android you can find, and be honest about whether you would stay.
tiktok.cap: Design for the hand they are holding, not the desk you are sitting at.

slides: Check it on a cheap Android
instagram.cap: The device in your pocket is not the device they have.

facebook.body:
Your website was designed on a laptop, probably while sitting down.

Your customer is holding a phone in one hand, in traffic, with 40% battery, deciding whether to bother.

Open your own site on the cheapest Android in your house. Not your phone. The old one. If you would not stay, they do not either.

When did you last look at your own site on a phone?

posts.topic: The thumb test
posts.why: A two-minute test they will actually run.

tiktok.hook: Hold your phone in one hand. Now buy from your site.
tiktok.vo: The thumb test. Hold your phone in one hand and try to buy from your own website. Can you reach the main button without moving your hand? Can you read the first line without zooming? Everything you cannot reach with a thumb is a customer who left. Move the button up and make the text bigger. That is the whole fix.
tiktok.cap: One hand. One thumb. Everything else is decoration.

instagram.cap: Run the thumb test on your own site tonight. It takes two minutes and it will annoy you.

facebook.body:
Try the thumb test tonight.

Hold your phone in one hand. Open your own website. Now try to buy something without moving your hand or using a second finger.

Can you reach the main button? Can you read the first line without zooming in?

Everything you cannot reach with a thumb is a customer who left quietly. Move the button up. Make the text bigger.

How did you do?

posts.topic: An entrance animation is a tax
posts.why: A position that will annoy designers and delight business owners.

tiktok.hook: An animation that delays your price is a tax on your customer.
tiktok.vo: An animation that delays your price is a tax on your customer. Two seconds of nothing, on mobile data, so that a heading can slide in. Motion is fine when it reveals something. When it delays the one thing they came for, it is decoration you are charging them for.
tiktok.cap: If the animation is between the customer and the price, it is a cost, not a design.

instagram.cap: Motion should reveal. If it delays, delete it.

facebook.body:
Hot take: entrance animations on a small business website are a tax on the customer.

Two seconds of nothing, on mobile data, so a heading can slide into place. Then the price appears.

Motion is good when it reveals something. When it stands between a customer and the one thing they came for, you are charging them for decoration.

What is the most annoying website animation you have seen?

posts.topic: She tapped the wrong thing twice
posts.why: A small failure with a big cost, which is the shape of most lost sales.

tiktok.hook: She gave up on a shop because the page jumped.
tiktok.vo: A woman gave up on a shop because the page kept jumping. An image loaded late, pushed everything down, and she tapped the delivery fee twice. Then a pop-up opened. She closed the lot and bought from someone with an uglier site that stayed still. You do not lose customers to design. You lose them to movement.
tiktok.cap: You do not lose customers to ugly design. You lose them to movement.

instagram.cap: Reserve space for every image. A page that jumps is a page that loses sales.

facebook.body:
A woman gave up on a shop because the page kept jumping.

An image loaded late and pushed everything down. She tapped the delivery fee twice by accident. A pop-up opened. She closed the whole thing and bought from a shop with an uglier website that stayed still.

You do not lose customers to ugly. You lose them to movement.

Has a jumpy page ever made you give up?

posts.topic: Compress before you upload
posts.why: The single highest-return technical fix in the whole month.

tiktok.hook: You do not need a developer. Stop uploading 4MB photos.
tiktok.vo: You do not need a developer to make your site faster. You need to stop uploading four megabyte photos. Resize to sixteen hundred pixels wide, compress to under two hundred kilobytes, and do it before you upload. Ten photos will take you twenty minutes and your page will load twice as fast.
tiktok.cap: Resize, compress, then upload. In that order, every time.

instagram.cap: Ten photos, twenty minutes, twice the speed. No developer needed.

facebook.body:
You do not need a developer to make your site load faster. You need to stop uploading 4MB photos straight from your camera.

Resize to about 1600 pixels wide. Compress to under 200KB. Then upload.

Ten photos is twenty minutes of work and it will roughly halve your load time.

Most 'slow website' problems in Nigeria are three photos nobody resized.

What is the biggest image on your site right now?

posts.topic: The caption bar is eating your button
posts.why: A five-second fix that most sites have never done.

tiktok.hook: The caption bar is sitting on top of your only button.
tiktok.vo: The caption bar is sitting on top of your only button. On most phones, the bottom sixty pixels are covered by a bar or a set of buttons. If your order button lives there, nobody can press it. Move it up and test again.
tiktok.cap: The bottom 60 pixels of a phone belong to the platform, not to you.

instagram.cap: Check where your button lands on an actual phone, not in the preview.

facebook.body:
Small thing that costs businesses real money: the bottom 60-80 pixels of a phone screen.

That strip belongs to the browser or the platform. If your main button sits there, a stranger physically cannot press it, and you will never know because it looks fine in the preview.

Open your site on a real phone. Look at where the button lands. Move it up.

Five seconds of work.

posts.topic: The last three shops you left
posts.why: The answers are the argument, and nobody can argue with them.

tiktok.hook: What were the last three shops you gave up on online?
tiktok.vo: What were the last three shops you gave up on online? Too slow. Would not load. Kept freezing. Three people, three answers, all the same answer. Not one of them said the site was ugly or expensive. They left because it made them wait.
tiktok.cap: Nobody on this street left because a shop was ugly. They left because it made them wait.

instagram.cap: Speed is the only design decision every customer notices.

facebook.body:
I asked people on the street: what were the last three shops you gave up on online?

Too slow. Would not load. Kept freezing.

Not one of them said the site was ugly. Not one said it was too expensive. They left because it made them wait.

All the design choices in the world do not matter if the page takes nine seconds.

What made you abandon a site?

instagram.cap: Buy it for confusion, not for speed. ₦5,000. Message CLEAR on WhatsApp: 0905 069 0837.

facebook.body:
If your website is slow, do not buy my homepage blueprint.

It is a writing pack. It fixes the first screen — what you say, in what order, and what the button does. It does not touch loading speed, hosting or image sizes.

Buy it if strangers read your page and still cannot tell what you sell. That is a words problem, and words are cheap to fix.

₦5,000. Message CLEAR on WhatsApp: 0905 069 0837.

What does your first screen say right now?

posts.topic: Fast on 2G, in three weeks
posts.why: A story about scope, told with the number that ends the conversation.

tiktok.hook: They wanted two seconds on 2G, in three weeks.
beats: We said no to the 2G part
We said yes to two seconds on 3G
tiktok.vo: Someone asked us to make their site load in two seconds on 2G, in three weeks. We said no to the 2G part. Two seconds on a good 3G connection is achievable and we can measure it. On 2G, nobody loads anything in two seconds, and we are not going to promise a number we cannot test. They took the version we could prove.
tiktok.cap: Say the number you can measure. Refuse the one you cannot.

slides: Yes, and we can prove it
instagram.cap: A promise you cannot measure is not a standard. It is a delay before the argument.

facebook.body:
Someone asked us to make their site load in two seconds on 2G, in three weeks.

We said no to the 2G part. Two seconds on a decent 3G connection is achievable and measurable. On 2G, nobody loads anything in two seconds, and promising it just delays the argument to delivery day.

They took the version we could prove.

The next time someone promises you a number, ask them how they will measure it.

Have you ever been promised a result nobody could measure?

posts.topic: Test on a real phone, on data
posts.why: One line that invalidates every comfortable test they have done.

tiktok.hook: Wifi lies to you every single time.
tiktok.vo: Wifi lies to you. Your office connection is faster than any customer's, and your browser has already saved the images. So the page you test is not the page they get. Turn off wifi, use mobile data, open in a private window, and count again. That is the real number.
tiktok.cap: Turn off wifi. Private window. Mobile data. Then look.

instagram.cap: Private window, mobile data, real phone. Any other test is fiction.

facebook.body:
Two things lie to you when you test your own website: your wifi and your browser cache.

Your office connection is faster than any customer's. Your browser has already saved the images, so the page you see is not the page they get.

Turn off wifi. Use mobile data. Open a private window. Now count the seconds.

That is the real number, and it is usually about twice what you thought.

What did yours turn out to be?
